body: @flozano can you show me the code where you add the handler ?
@flozano quick question. Is this done from the EventLoop thread or not ?
also was the "ChannelHandlerConstant.MQTT_DECODER_HANDLER_NAME" added with a custom ChannelHandlerInvoker or EventExecutorGroup.
@flozano also when you say these are locked are these never recover ?

Yes, the full stack-trace shows `setIdle` as invoked in threads `mqtt-netty-worker-3-1` and `mqtt-netty-worker-3-2.`, which are the NioEventLoopGroup threads:

``` java
return new NioEventLoopGroup(0, new DefaultThreadFactory("mqtt-netty-worker"));
```

the `ChannelHandlerConstant.MQTT_DECODER_HANDLER_NAME` was added in the ChannelInitializer as:

``` java
p.addLast(MQTT_DECODER_HANDLER_NAME, new MqttDecoder(brokerSettings.getMaxPayloadSize()));
```

so nothing special there either.

> @flozano also when you say these are locked are these never recover ?

Yeah, no recovery in sight, the server gets fully locked.

@flozano I tried to reproduce here but no luck with a unit test. Any way I can reproduce this easily ?
We haven't isolated the issue yet I'm afraid, we can try
I found that the issue occurs as of version 4.1.0.CR3, in version 4.1.0.CR2 it is working fine.

@flozano from the stack trace may it be possible that while the thread is an EventLoop thread it may be possible that the addBefore(...) call is done in an EventLoop that not belongs to the Channel and so it's pipeline ?
We have only one eventLoop instance in the server for the worker threads, so I think is not possible that the Channel belongs to another one.
@johnou this is strange as the posted stack can only happen when the pipeline operation is executed from outside the EventLoop that belongs to it. And from what @flozano said you have 2 threads.
